title: No time to exercise: a 20-minute plan for working women
intro: You don't need an hour at the gym to start seeing changes. 20 minutes is enough to start. Combine it with controlled eating, and realistic weight loss of an estimated 0.5 to 1 kg a week is achievable.

sections.h: Why 20 minutes is enough to start
sections.p: Short but consistent workouts are better than long ones once in a while. Strength training helps you keep your muscle while you lose weight. It also helps your body feel more energetic for daily work.

5 minutes of warm-up, for example marching on the spot and shoulder rolls. 12 minutes of circuit: squats, push-ups against a wall or table, lunges, glute bridges and plank, each for 40 seconds with 20 seconds of rest. Finish with 3 minutes of stretching.
Do this circuit 3 days a week, for example Monday, Wednesday and Friday. On other days, just walking is enough. If you miss a day, just continue the next day without guilt.

Walking to the mamak, taking the stairs at the office or walking during phone calls all add to your daily activity. Aim for an estimated 7,000 to 8,000 steps a day, building up gradually. This helps without needing special time.
If you are pregnant, have heart problems, joint pain or other health conditions, get your doctor's advice before starting. Start slowly and increase the intensity once your body gets used to it.

action: Pick 3 days this week and put 20 minutes of exercise in your calendar like a meeting.
Try the 20-minute circuit once at light intensity.
Take the stairs at least one floor every workday.
Check your daily steps on your phone and add 1,000 steps to your usual.
myth: Many believe doing lots of sit-ups will burn belly fat. In fact, your body can't choose where to lose fat; fat reduces overall when you eat in a controlled way and stay active consistently.

faq.q: Do I need to join a gym?
faq.a: No need. This 20-minute circuit can be done at home, in a hotel room when outstation, or in a small space at the office.

faq.q: How fast will I see results?
faq.a: Everyone is different. Many start feeling more energetic within 2 to 3 weeks, and changes in body shape usually take a few weeks or months.

faq.q: My knees hurt, what should I do?
faq.a: Reduce the depth of your squats or use a chair as a guide, and avoid jumping. If the pain continues, see a doctor or physiotherapist.
